body.text: You will have had the Chancellor's letter. Everybody has had the Chancellor's letter; he read it aloud at dinner.

I will not pretend the ground can be held from here, because there is nothing left on it to hold. But ground can be settled twice. I can have a company of settlers aboard the Crown's ships within the season — guards, stores, a surgeon, the whole business — and in five months they will be on the coast where your towns were, with nothing done to them on the way.
The Crown will carry them as long as it is still honouring your word. It will not carry them on anything less, and it will not ask twice.

What they arrive as depends on what you put behind them. {param:amount} for the handsome version: stores enough, tools, and a granary standing before the first winter. Less for less. Or you may let it go, and I will understand, and I will think less of the arrangement.

tone.text: On a second landing I am {choice}.

options.text: grateful beyond what I can easily say

options.label: equip it handsomely
options.text: Send them properly found. If the colony is to begin again, it will not begin poor.

options.label: equip it adequately
options.text: Enough to stand it up, and no more. They may earn the rest.

options.label: send them with what you can spare
options.text: Send them. I cannot furnish them, and I will not pretend it is generous, but I will not let it end here.

options.label: let it go
options.text: Let it go. I will not send more people to a coast that has already taken everyone we sent.

closing.text: I am, sir, your obedient servant,
